narrative:
On August 29, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 43.8%, resolving 907 cases out of 2,069 scheduled across 46 judges. This represents a slight efficiency improvement compared to the previous day’s rate of 42.2% (1,102 heard of 2,611 scheduled on August 28) and a notable rise from the 37.7% registered on August 27. However, the clearance rate remains marginally below the week's peak of 44.2% observed on August 25.

Individual docket clearances varied widely by bench. Justice Suraj Govindaraj in Hall 11 demonstrated high efficiency, hearing 33 of 39 scheduled cases (84.6%). Similarly, the division bench of Justice R. Devdas and Justice K. Manmadha Rao in Hall 5 achieved an 82.0% clearance rate, hearing 41 of 50 matters. Conversely, Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad in Hall 6, burdened with a massive block of 268 scheduled cases, was able to hear only one (0.4%), though he resolved 10 of 25 cases (40.0%) listed in a separate session. 

Writ Petitions (WP) dominated the day's docket with 1,005 scheduled cases, securing a 37.9% hearing rate. Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) and Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) saw stronger clearance rates at 61.9% (197 of 318) and 54.4% (135 of 248), respectively. In terms of hearing stages, "Orders" constituted the largest share with 810 scheduled cases and a 41.1% conversion rate—a slight drop from the 45.4% recorded on August 28. "Admission" stages achieved the highest progress at 56.7% (144 of 254), while "Final Hearing" matters registered a 36.0% hearing rate (113 of 314).
